properties.areaDesc: Greater Lake Tahoe Area; Greater Lake Tahoe Area
properties.headline: Avalanche Watch issued November 18 at 9:10AM PST by NWS Reno NV
properties.description:
AVAREV

The following message is transmitted at the request of the U.S.
Forest Service Sierra Avalanche Center.

BACKCOUNTRY AVALANCHE WATCH

IMMEDIATE BROADCAST REQUESTED

08:55 PST Wed Nov 18 2026

The Sierra Avalanche Center in Truckee has issued a BACKCOUNTRY
AVALANCHE WATCH for the following areas:
NWS Reno NV - NVZ002 (Greater Lake Tahoe)...CAZ072 (Greater Lake Tahoe (CA))

* WHAT...HIGH avalanche danger is anticipated in the backcountry
from around sunset on Wednesday into early Friday morning.

* WHERE...Central Sierra Nevada Mountains between Yuba Pass (Hwy
49) on the north and Ebbetts Pass(Hwy 4) on the south,
including the greater Lake Tahoe area. This applies only to
backcountry areas, not to ski areas and highways where avalanche
mitigation programs exist.

* WHEN...In effect from Wed 08:55 PST to Thu 05:00 PST.

* IMPACTS...Significant snowfall may lead to widespread avalanche
activity in the mountains. Large avalanches capable of burying
or injuring people could occur in backcountry areas.

* PRECAUTIONARY / PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...Very dangerous
avalanche conditions could occur in the backcountry. Traveling
in, near, or below backcountry avalanche terrain during HIGH
avalanche danger is not recommended.

Consult https://www.sierraavalanchecenter.org/ or
www.avalanche.org for more detailed information.

Similar avalanche danger may exist at locations outside
the coverage area of this or any avalanche center.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Marine Weather Statement issued November 18 at 11:29AM EST by NWS Key West FL
properties.description:
At 1130 am, widespread showers are ongoing across the Florida Keys
and surrounding near and offshore waters within a mesoscale
convective complex. This activity is producing pockets of higher
wind gusts of 25 to near 34 knots and reduced visibility from
moderate to heavy downpours. Lightning frequency is decreasing
substantially. Activity is slowly propagating eastward and
circulating around a small scale area of low pressure currently
centered in the Straits of Florida approximately 32 nautical miles
southeast of Key West. Showers are diminishing from west to east, and
rain has ended in the waters near Key West, but strong to briefly
gale force easterly wind gusts are occurring along the western
periphery of the decaying precipitation near the Lower Keys.

breakpoints along the coast from this afternoon through Friday
morning.

and rocks.

and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively.

properties.areaDesc: Ventura County Beaches
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 18 at 7:48AM PST until November 20 at 9:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large breaking waves of 8 to 12 feet with dangerous rip
currents.

* WHERE...Ventura County Beaches.

* WHEN...From 9 PM this evening to 9 PM PST Friday. Peak surf
expected Thursday.

* IMPACTS...There is an increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip
currents can pull swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large
breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and
rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Pooling of sea
water is possible around high tide at beach and harbor areas
that is uncommon with normal tidal ranges. Enhanced beach
erosion is also possible. No significant damage is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Minor coastal flooding may occur near early
morning high tide. Additional hazardous surf and coastal
flooding isues are expected next week.
properties.instruction:
Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Breaking waves

and coastal flooding isues are expected next week.

near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in

properties.instruction:

Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued November 18 at 7:06AM PST by NWS Spokane WA
properties.description:
Patchy dense fog has been observed across portions of the Spokane
and Coeur d'Alene metro this this morning, especially northern
Spokane County and the West Plains, including I-90 and US-2.
Within fog, expect visibilities as low as one-quarter mile. Use
extra caution while traveling as visibilities can change quickly.
If fog is encountered, use low-beam headlights and keep plenty of
space between you and other vehicles. The fog is expected to lift
by mid-morning.

THIS EVENING DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR PORTIONS OF
CENTRAL AND SOUTH CENTRAL NEBRASKA...

* AFFECTED AREA...Portions of central and south central Nebraska.

* TIMING...From noon today to 6 PM CST this evening.

* WINDS...westerly, with sustained speeds around 20 MPH and gusts
around 25-30 MPH.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...as low as 20-25 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of strong winds,
low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can contribute to
extreme fire behavior.

properties.headline: Winter Weather Advisory issued November 18 at 5:48AM AKST until November 18 at 4:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Freezing rain and rain on ice will cause slick road and
sidewalk conditions. Mixed precipitation may bring a light glaze of
ice to surfaces.

* WHERE...Anchorage / Eagle River (all elevations), Lower Matanuska
Valley, NW Kenai Peninsula, Interior Kenai Peninsula, and Turnagain
Pass.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM AKST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. The hazardous conditions
will impact the Wednesday morning commute.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The incoming front is moving faster and has
already warmed up many areas above freezing. The hazards from
freezing rain and rain falling on frozen surfaces should be mainly
over for the whole area by early afternoon. TUrnagain Pass through
Summit Pass along the Seward Highway may see 4 to 7 inches of
snowfall from this system before turning to rain.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. For the latest road
conditions call 5 1 1 or visit 511.alaska.gov.

Be prepared for slippery roads. Slow down and use caution while
driving. If you are going outside, watch your first few steps taken
on stairs, sidewalks, and driveways. These surfaces could be icy and
slippery, increasing your risk of a fall and injury.

concentrations within the region may become unhealthy for sensitive
groups. Sensitive groups include children, the elderly, and people

properties.areaDesc: Pribilof Islands
properties.headline: High Wind Warning issued November 18 at 4:11AM AKST until November 18 at 9:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Southwest winds 45 to 55 mph with gusts up to 75 mph.

* WHERE...Pribilof Islands.

* WHEN...Until 9 AM AKST this morning.

* IMPACTS...High winds may move loose debris, damage property, and
cause power outages. Travel will be difficult.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Winds gusting to 75 mph early this morning for
both St. Paul and St. George. As a result of the long duration of
westerly winds, wave heights of 25 to 30 ft within 15 to 20
nautical miles of Saint Paul are expected through Wednesday
afternoon.

Ongoing precipitation has been observed as a rain/snow mix. In
conjunction with strong winds, visibility may drop to as low as
one-half mile at times in stronger snow showers Wednesday morning.
properties.instruction:
People are urged to secure loose objects that could be blown around
or damaged by the wind. Prepare for the possibility of widespread
power outages. Use caution if you must drive.

NWSheadline: HIGH WIND WARNING REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 9 AM AKST THIS MORNING

properties.areaDesc: Pribilof Islands
properties.headline: High Surf Advisory issued November 18 at 4:07AM AKST until November 18 at 12:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Large waves of 25 to 30 feet may impact Saint Paul,
including the harbor area.

* WHERE...West Saint Paul

* WHEN...Until Noon AKST today.

* IMPACTS...Large waves may result in water overtopping the
breakwater at Saint Paul Harbor, leading to minor flooding of
low-lying coastal areas, particularly near the harbor. Coastal
erosion is possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Prolonged gusty westerly winds will
continue through this morning as the storm weakens and shifts
the core of strongest winds to the north. Winds and seas will
diminish through this afternoon.
properties.instruction:
Precautions should be taken to protect property. Stay away from
beaches, shorelines, and harbor areas.

NWSheadline: HIGH SURF ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL NOON AKST TODAY

properties.areaDesc: Kuskokwim Delta Coast and Nunivak Island
properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 18 at 4:07AM AKST until November 18 at 9:00AM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Coastal Flooding with water levels of 1.0 to 3.0 feet
above the highest tide line possible.

* WHERE...Kipnuk and Kwigillingok

* WHEN...3 AM to 9 AM AKST today.

* IMPACTS...Potential flooding of low lying areas, including
overtop the lowest portions of boardwalks. Coastal erosion
possible.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A long duration of gusty southerly winds
moved through the Kuskokwim Coast yesterday. Winds have shifted
more south to southwesterly this morning, increasing the
potential for elevated water levels, high surf, and coastal
erosion. The winds will coincide with the high tide this morning.
properties.instruction:
A coastal flood advisory indicates that onshore winds and tides
will combine to generate flooding of low areas along the shore.

NWSheadline: COASTAL FLOOD ADVISORY REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 9 AM AKST THIS MORNING

properties.areaDesc: North Bay Interior Mountains
properties.headline: Flash Flood Watch issued November 18 at 4:46AM PST until November 19 at 12:00AM PST by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding and debris flows caused by excessive rainfall
continue to be possible over the Pickett burn area.

* WHERE...Areas northeast of Calistoga in Napa County.

* WHEN...Through this evening.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Pickett burn area is expected
during the period of the watch. Residents near the Pickett burn
area should prepare for potential debris flow moving through the
Simmons Canyon and areas near and between Pickett Road to Silverado
Trail. Be sure to stay up to date with information from local
authorities. Heavy rainfall could trigger flash flooding of
low-lying areas, roadway flooding, and debris flows in and near
recent wildfire burn scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- National Weather Service Meteorologists are forecasting heavy
rainfall over the Timber and Plaskett burn areas, which may lead
to flash flooding and debris flows.
- Some locations that may experience flash flooding include...
Areas northeast of Calistoga.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

Local emergency services are monitoring the situation and will issue
a public statement as conditions warrant. PLAN NOW so you will know
what to do in an emergency. Keep informed by listening to local radio
and television for statements and possible warnings. Follow the
advice of public safety officials.

properties.description:

are possible over the Plaskett and Timber burn areas.

* WHERE...For the Timber Scar, portions of CA Highway 1 and the Los
Padres National Forecast from Andrew Molera State Park to
Partington Ridge including the town of Big Sur.

For the Plaskett Scar, areas near CA Highway 1 mile marker 17 to mile
marker 11 including Los Burros Road.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Heavy rainfall over the Timber and Plaskett burn areas is
expected during the watch period. Residents near the Timber burn
area should prepare for potential debris flow moving through the
drainages within Lafler, Castro, and Graves Canyons, as well as
drainages between Grimes and Castro Canyons.

Residents near the Plaskett burn area should prepare for potential
debris flow moving through the Alder, Plaskett, and Prewitt Creeks.

Thursday noon.

* WHEN...Until 10 AM PST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Conditions will be hazardous to small craft,
especially when operating near to, or attempting to cross, the

Bar. Mariners are advised to obtain the latest bar conditions
from the United States Coast Guard before attempting to cross the
bar.

taking shelter in port until hazardous seas subside.

hazardous conditions will impact the Wednesday morning and evening
commutes. Gusty winds could bring down tree branches. Roads, and
especially bridges and overpasses, will likely become slick and
hazardous. The strong winds and weight of snow on tree limbs may
down power lines and could cause sporadic power outages.
properties.instruction:
Slow down and use caution while traveling. The latest road conditions
for the state you are calling from can be obtained by calling 5 1 1.

Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.

properties.headline: Red Flag Warning issued November 18 at 2:32AM MST until November 18 at 5:00PM MST by NWS Cheyenne WY
properties.description:
...RED FLAG WARNING IN EFFECT FROM 9 AM THIS MORNING TO 5 PM MST THIS
AFTERNOON DUE TO WIND AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY FOR PORTIONS OF NE
AND WY...

The National Weather Service in Cheyenne WY has issued a Red Flag
Warning in effect from 9 AM this morning to 5 PM MST this afternoon.

* AFFECTED AREA...In southeast Wyoming, fire weather zones 430
through 433. In western Nebraska, fire weather zones 436 and 437.

* TIMING...From 9 AM this morning to 5 PM MST this afternoon.

* WINDS...West winds 25 to 40 mph with gusts up to 65 mph in Wyoming
and up to 55 mph in Nebraska.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Relative Humidity between 14 and 20 percent.

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning is issued when we identify weather conditions that
promote rapid spread of fire which may become life-threatening. This
does not mean there is a fire. These conditions are either occurring
now or will begin soon. It is important to have multiple ways to
receive information from authorities.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 18 at 2:01AM CST until November 19 at 6:00AM CST by NWS Brownsville TX
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 4
to 5 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor
coastal flooding.

* WHERE...Kenedy Island, Willacy Island and Cameron Island
Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 6 PM CST Thursday.
For the High Rip Current Risk, through Thursday afternoon. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 6 AM CST Thursday.

* IMPACTS...Nuisance flooding is expected, with water reaching or
pushing into the dunes on South Padre Island. Vehicles, except
those with four wheel drive and high wheel bases, will be unable
to be driven on the beach. This includes locations north of
Public Beach Access #3. Minor to moderate beach erosion is
expected. Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
If travel is required, allow extra time as some roads may be
closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Inexperienced swimmers should remain out of the water due to
dangerous surf conditions.

Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the
shore and call or wave for help.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 5
to 10 feet in the surf zone. For the High Rip Current Risk,
dangerous rip currents.

* WHERE...Coastal Volusia, Coastal Indian River, Coastal Saint
Lucie, Coastal Martin, Mainland Northern Brevard, Northern
Brevard Barrier Islands, Mainland Southern Brevard and
Southern Brevard Barrier Islands Counties.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 7 PM EST Friday. For
the High Rip Current Risk, through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous swimming and surfing conditions and
localized beach erosion. Rip currents can sweep even the best
swimmers away from shore into deeper water.
properties.instruction:
High surf will affect the beaches in the advisory area, producing
localized beach erosion and dangerous swimming conditions.
Swimmers should remain out of the water due to large breaking
waves and dangerous surf conditions.

Rip currents are powerful channels of water flowing quickly away
from shore, which occur most often at low spots or breaks in the
sandbar and in the vicinity of structures such as jetties and
piers. Heed the advice of lifeguards, beach patrol flags and
signs.

Entering the surf is strongly discouraged. If caught in a rip
current, relax and float. Don't swim against the current. If
able, swim in a direction following the shoreline. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

properties.areaDesc: SW Kenai Peninsula
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 17 at 1:32PM AKST until November 19 at 6:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by rain on
snow is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following area, SW Kenai Peninsula. This
includes the cities of Homer, Anchor Point, Ninilchik, And Clam
Gulch.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Flooding may occur in poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An atmospheric river event is anticipated to begin Wednesday
morning, with ample moisture transport from the south. With
upslope enhancement, most areas are on track to see 2 to 3 inches
of rainfall from this system, with locally higher amounts with
elevation. Heaviest rainfall rates will occur between Wednesday
afternoon and Thursday morning with about a quarter of an inch
per 3 hour period. This amount of rainfall on the new snowpack
may cause flooding along smaller streams and creeks, in low-lying
and poor drainage areas, and cause ponding of water on roadways.
Rainfall is on track to decrease Thursday.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.areaDesc: Southern Kenai Mtns
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 17 at 1:32PM AKST until November 19 at 6:00PM AKST by NWS Anchorage AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Small stream and localized urban flooding caused by
excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Including the following area, Southern Kenai Mtns. This
includes the city of Seward.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.
Storm drains and ditches may become clogged with debris. Flooding
may occur in poor drainage areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- An atmospheric river event is anticipated to begin Wednesday
morning, with ample moisture transport from the south. With
upslope enhancement, most areas are on track to see 2 to 4 inches
of rainfall from this system, with locally higher amounts with
elevation. Rainfall rates of up to a quarter of an inch per hour
are possible between 3PM Wednesday through 3PM Thursday.
Southerly to southeasterly winds will shift to more easterly
early Thursday morning, limiting precipitation amounts in lee of
the mountains for areas along the Seward Highway from roughly
Moose Pass and southward to Seward. Rainfall is on track to
decrease late Thursday afternoon. Prolonged heavy rain may lead
to areas of flooding along smaller streams and creeks, in
low-lying and poor drainage areas, and ponding of water on
roadways.

- Http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Stay tuned to further developments by listening to your local radio,
television, or NOAA Weather Radio for further information.

You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

suffering from asthma, heart disease, or other lung diseases. The

exercise or strenuous activity.

properties.headline: Flood Watch issued November 16 at 3:18PM EST until November 20 at 7:00PM EST by NWS Melbourne FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...Most of east central Florida, including Volusia, Seminole,
Orange, Osceola, Okeechobee, Brevard, Indian River, Saint Lucie,
and Martin counties.

* WHEN...From Tuesday afternoon through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Repeated rounds of showers and isolated storms are forecast
through Friday. Rainfall amounts of 3 to 6 inches are forecast
with localized higher amounts of 8 to 12 inches. The greatest
potential for these higher amounts will be over the coastal
counties.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH IN EFFECT FROM TUESDAY AFTERNOON THROUGH FRIDAY EVENING
